d: Slightly turned or opened; as, the door was standing ajar.
w.e: OE. on char ajar, on the turn; AS. cerr, cyrr, turn, akin to G. kehren to turn, and to D. akerre. See Char.

d: In a state of discord; out of harmony; as, he is ajar with the world.
A tube through which is water is discharged; an efflux tube; as, the ajutage of a fountain.
w.e: F. ajutage, for ajoutage, fr. ajouter to add, LL. adjuxtare, fr. L. ad + juxta near to, nigh. Cf. Adjutage, Adjustage, Adjust.
